Privacy and power

Attackers claim 147 GB of Revolut data

A forged Italian government order reportedly opened the bank’s customer files, and the compliance rules gave it no good way to tell.

The lead

The Revolut breach moved from alarm to anatomy overnight. Lyudmyla Kozlovska says the attackers first took over Italian government and law-enforcement mailboxes, then sent the Lithuanian bank a forged European Investigation Order over five months.

According to Kozlovska’s account, Revolut answered each request because FATF recommendations and European anti-money-laundering rules require it to answer state requests. The rules can punish refusal with fines of up to €5 million or 10 per cent of turnover, while requiring no reliable check that the state behind a request is the state it claims to be.

Every bank, exchange, payment provider and #CASP in every jurisdiction that follows FATF rules is exposed the same way

The attackers say the Italian side of the haul is 147 GB, including internal documents and officer chat logs, and that passports and KYC selfies are being published while they demand payment. The claims are still claims; the exposure described is not a theoretical one.

Kozlovska’s remedy is political: put the safeguards rejected by the European Commission and Council back into the rules, before the next leak names someone who does not have the means to move house.

The physical world

The next storm is already in the plans

A shoreline project advances while the person watching it expects the first serious weather to undo much of the work.

A photograph

The day’s picture-led story is a small argument with permanence. BitBees reports that a wharf is coming along while the people on the far side build a beach beside it.

The judgment is unsentimental: the sand may be gone with the first storm, and the bulkhead may not survive it. There is no grand lesson attached, only the useful scale of a person looking at a project and already measuring it against the weather.

Software desk

Flotilla trades the home page for an inbox

Flotilla’s new release is large enough to be a product reset: a dashboard of unread conversations, space activity and a network feed replaces the old home page.

The redesign also gives calendars month, week and agenda views with RSVPs, turns classifieds into a browsable marketplace, keeps direct messages through relay retention, and adds a desktop package for Linux, Windows and macOS.

The release carries the usual warning label. Its author calls this the first primarily clanker-written version, a mixture of bug fixes, flashy features and busy work. The useful part is the list of things now visible in one place: voice dictation and read-aloud, relay import and export, muted rooms, link-preview fallbacks and an end-to-end test suite.

Fiatjaf’s field report found an unfinished edge: the new user path works, while identity import does nothing, and repository tabs need a way to close. The release is live on Zapstore and the web; iOS and Play Store packages are due later.

Security desk

Bisq 2 puts Tor on the update path

Bisq 2 version 2.1.13 bundles the latest Tor security release. The announcement treats the update as a condition of continuing to trade.

Updating to this version is required to continue trading.

Freedom.Tech’s release board places the patch at the head of a privacy-heavy list that also includes Cashu TS, BitBoxApp and other wallet updates. The day’s lesson is plain and unglamorous: the software that keeps a private system useful still needs maintenance.

Foundation is making a different kind of maintenance possible. Legacy Mode is in beta on Passport Prime, bringing supported open-source Ledger apps to KeyOS. Existing recovery phrases, addresses and balances can remain where they are while compatible software wallets connect over USB.

The relay question

A free relay still sends someone the bill

Fiatjaf asks why anyone would pay to write to a random relay when free public ones already exist. The answer he finds is not storage alone, but the quality of the view.

A paid or invited relay could offer cleaner feeds, more dependable threads and a place where the people reading actually chose the signal. At Nostr’s current size, he says, cheap whitelisted relays may be enough; the missing piece is that few people know a good feed is something they can pay for.

That is a small economic question with a large product hidden inside it: who is responsible for the room a reader opens?

Tools with boundaries

The wallet that declines to spend

Ashigaru Desktop receives and mixes. Spending stays on mobile or in another wallet that can read the same file.

Stay in your lane and there is less of you to attack.

Its useful feature, Ungovernable argues, is the absent one: a watch-only wallet can send coinjoin outputs to a fresh hardware-wallet address after a chosen number of mixes, without a manual transfer or a copied address.

Voca 1.2 takes the same shape in a different room. Slow Android speech engines no longer create long pauses, and its anonymous diagnostics report is explicitly opt-in, shown before sending, with document text excluded unless separately enabled for that report.

In brief · On the calendar · The day in numbers

In brief

My First Bitcoin says its independent education network now supports educators with open-source resources and infrastructure, funded by the community it serves.

Routstr says it has sunset its official node after a month and a half without a visible service break; its nodes are now community-run and discovered through Nostr.

Signed, an early collaboration client for Nostr Git and Grasp Protocol, is available as an alpha for macOS, Windows, Linux and the web to come. reya announced it as a project that wants feedback while it is still rough.

From the picture desk

Worth the scroll

One of the longer technical notes proposes cold-storage identities for Nostr: keys created in cold storage and kept away from internet-connected devices while still usable for everyday signing.

Another asks what a good restaurant platform would look like if the restaurant kept its customer list and did not surrender a cut of every ticket. Different desks, the same question: can the tool serve the person using it?
